newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy PM gets report on key cost controls - Sole.
newsitem.headline: Italy PM gets report on key cost controls - Sole.

text.p: The office of Prime Minister Romano Prodi has received a report citing ministries that must control spending in late 1997 to ensure Italy qualifies for European economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999, daily Il Sole newspaper said on Sunday.
The detailed government report cited public education, public employment, posts, transport, health and defence as the sectors most at risk of overspending, Il Sole said.
Italy is striving to stick to planned spending cuts to keep its 1997 budget deficit-to-gross domestic product ratio down at the 3.0 percent level required for joining EMU.
Il Sole said the working group on monitoring public finances, set up at the start of the year by the Treasury, passed the detailed report to Prodi's office.

Il Sole said the report stated: "Above all in the final phase of the year it is very important that those responsible for individual administrations and ministries keep the state of corrective financial measures constantly under control and the level of cash distribution in each ministry for the close of the financial year."
